page: Microsoft Azure E4bs_v5 is an EBSv5-family virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this server utilizes a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 48 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on remote Premium Storage capabilities for block storage performance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core performance alongside constrained multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the server in the average tier, while multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register in the lower quartile, though Passmark memory scores remain average. Cryptographic execution, such as Passmark CPU encryption, and single-threaded compression tasks perform at an average level, whereas multi-threaded decompression and database operations show weaker throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4bs_v5 offers an elevated memory-to-vCPU density, making it applicable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. Given the lack of local storage and the average single-core performance, this virtual machine is appropriate for workloads such as small-scale database hosting, memory-cached applications, and text processing tasks that benefit from 32 GB of RAM but do not saturate multi-core compute resources.
